item.title: BC Blows Out Washington, Goes 2–1 in the 2026 Puerto Rico Challenge
item.description: Boston College men's baseball travelled to Ponce, Puerto Rico for the Puerto Rico Challenge to start its 2026 season. The Eagles came out of the weekend with a 2–1 record, including a 10–0 run-rule victory over Washington.

item.title: “Sharing Lou’s Story”: Susan Michalczyk Awarded for Documentaries Preserving Lou Montgomery’s Legacy
item.description: “We honor the Red Bandanna every year,” Michalczyk said. “Why don’t we honor Lou?”

item.title: Purpose Through Service: A Guide To Giving Back at BC
item.description: Service is an integral piece of Boston College’s mission to form “men and women for others.” But with so many different volunteering opportunities, how do you know what type of service is the right fit for you?

item.title: How to Care for Your Winter Clothing
item.description: By now, you’ve (hopefully) figured out how to properly dress to brave the winter weather, whether it be wind, rain, sleet, or snow. Caring for your winter clothing, though? That’s a whole other challenge.

item.title: Please Get Weirder: On Cookie-Cutter Culture
item.description: I know my nerds, geeks, and artsy kids are out there, but we’re often quiet about it. Why? I have a handful of theories.

item.title: Eagles Blow 14-Point Second-Half Lead, Fall 80–72 to Florida State
item.description: Despite leading by 12 points with 9:19 to play, the Eagles (9–17, 2–11 Atlantic Coast) fell 80–72 in Tallahassee as Florida State (13–13, 6–7) handed BC its seventh consecutive loss. BC has not lost seven straight games since the 2016-17 season, which it finished on a 15-game losing streak.

item.title: UGBC Discusses Issues With Magnet Initiative, Continues To Explore Advising Match Form
item.description: UGBC discussed the future of its magnet initiative on Tuesday, following distribution delays in several residence halls.

item.title: Pentagon Considering Graduate Tuition Aid Cuts for Active Service Members at Boston College
item.description: The Department of Defense (DOD) will review and potentially cut off tuition aid for active service members at Boston College and other elite universities nationwide that are no longer “committed to American values,” per a video statement from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
